canonical_identifiers.article_title: Sarconesin II, a New Antimicrobial Peptide Isolated from Sarconesiopsis magellanica Excretions and Secretions.
canonical_identifiers.source_organism: Sarconesiopsis magellanica larval excretions and secretions

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sarconesin II damages E. coli membrane integrity, supported by PI/CFDA fluorescence, PI microscopy, and SEM morphology assays at MIC exposure.
source_locators: xml:sec=13:2.6.2. Examining Bacterial Membrane Change by SEM

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8; xml:sec=10; xml:sec=13; xml:fig=6; xml:fig=8; xml:fig=10

mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Text reports increased PI/CFDA fluorescence, PI-positive treated cells, and SEM membrane disruption/blebbing after sarconesin II exposure.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct bacterial membrane damage evidence in E. coli; exact plotted fluorescence values were not needed for the claim and were not fabricated.
mechanism_claims.summary: Direct assays support membrane disruption in E. coli.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sarconesin II interacts with E. coli genomic DNA in vitro and is associated with reduced/partial DAPI fluorescence in treated bacteria.
source_locators: xml:sec=9:2.5.2. Sarconesin II Effects on E. coli DNA and Protein Profile
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Gel retardation tested 25, 50, and 100 µM peptide with 500 ng E. coli genomic DNA and reported suppressed migration; DAPI microscopy suggested DNA fragmentation.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct DNA-binding/fluorescence evidence, but does not quantify intracellular target specificity beyond the reported assays.
mechanism_claims.summary: Direct assays support DNA interaction/fragmentation context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sarconesin II did not visibly alter the E. coli total protein profile under the SDS-PAGE conditions reported, unlike the streptomycin control.
source_locators: xml:sec=9:2.5.2. Sarconesin II Effects on E. coli DNA and Protein Profile
xml:sec=28:4.10.3. Total Protein Profiling of E. coli Cells Treated with Sarconesin II
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Primary source reports sarconesin II-treated bacteria had the same protein profile as PBS control in Figure 7b.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: This is a negative boundary claim; it prevents overclaiming protein-profile disruption as sarconesin II mechanism.
mechanism_claims.summary: No direct protein-profile disruption was supported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sarconesin II showed alpha-helical secondary-structure propensity in TFE/CD and I-TASSER context, supporting biophysical characterization but not a standalone killing mechanism.
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: CD spectra varied with TFE and I-TASSER predicted an alpha helix; the helical wheel had no hydrophobic face reported.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Biophysical context only; not promoted to a direct antimicrobial MoA without the membrane/DNA assays.
mechanism_claims.summary: Secondary structure supports contextual biophysics, not an independent direct mechanism.

mechanism_summary: Sarconesin II has direct membrane-damage and DNA-interaction evidence in E. coli, with protein-profile disruption not supported and alpha-helical structure treated as context.
absence_and_boundary_notes: Do not treat the ATP synthase conserved-domain/source-protein context as a target mechanism of antimicrobial killing.
No exact figure-level fluorescence or microscopy quantification was fabricated from images.
Protein synthesis/profile disruption is not supported for sarconesin II under the reported SDS-PAGE assay.
source_exhaustion_notes: XML sections, PDF text, figure captions, OA package inventory, and methods were checked; no supplementary mechanism files are present.
